headline: Ressa and Gates Issue Separate Warnings as AI Governance Lags
seoTitle: Ressa, Gates Raise Separate Warnings Over AI Governance | FMB News
seoDescription: Maria Ressa urged stronger safeguards for human agency while Bill Gates said governments are unprepared for AI’s social effects, in separate warnings.
deck: Maria Ressa called for stronger safeguards to protect human agency, while Bill Gates separately warned that governments are not prepared for AI’s social effects.
author: FMB News Technology Desk

sections.heading: What happened
paragraphs: Journalist and Nobel Peace Prize laureate Maria Ressa and Microsoft co-founder Bill Gates issued separate warnings this week about the pace of artificial-intelligence development and the ability of governments to manage its effects.

In a Reuters interview, Ressa argued for stronger limits and accountability around AI systems, warning that unchecked development could erode human agency and worsen problems already associated with information manipulation and addictive digital systems.

In a separate Reuters interview, Gates said governments worldwide were not sufficiently prepared for AI-driven changes, pointing to risks involving jobs, attacks and addictive AI companions while also stressing the technology’s potential benefits.

sections.heading: Context
paragraphs: The two warnings were not part of a joint initiative and their prescriptions are not identical. Ressa emphasized regulation and protections for human agency, while Gates focused on government preparedness, international cooperation and equitable access to beneficial uses of AI.

The Gates Foundation said it plans to spend at least $1 billion over the next two years to expand access to AI applications and supporting data systems in areas including health, education and agriculture.

sections.heading: Why this matters
paragraphs: The debate is increasingly practical for the Philippines. AI is moving into workplaces, schools, media, customer service, public administration and consumer products faster than many institutions can update rules, skills and safeguards.

For a country with a large services workforce and substantial exposure to digital platforms, policy choices around reskilling, information integrity, cybersecurity, child and consumer protection, and access to useful AI tools can shape both the benefits and the disruptions.

sections.heading: What to watch next
paragraphs: Watch for concrete national and international rules on high-risk AI systems, transparency, platform accountability and the use of AI agents, rather than broad principles alone.
Also watch whether workforce and education policies keep pace with adoption, and whether access to useful AI systems expands beyond wealthy institutions and English-dominant users.
